en.title: Workplace Harassment: What Evidence Should You Keep?
en.directAnswer: If workplace conduct is harming or threatening you, protect your safety first. Keep a private factual record of dates, messages, emails, witnesses and reports made to HR or management. The correct legal route depends on the conduct. Some cases may involve labour law, workplace policy, civil rights or criminal offences.

en.lawMeaning:
This page should focus on evidence and safe reporting, not make a legal finding from one short description.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Use internal complaint route when safe.
Use police/legal help if there are threats, assault or other offences.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: An employee reports repeated threatening messages from a supervisor. Saving the original messages and a dated HR complaint is stronger than only telling colleagues verbally.
commonMistakes: deleting messages after screenshotting only part of the conversation..
en.specialistTrigger: Threats; sexual violence; assault; blackmail; retaliation; termination after complaint.
